title: Affective prosody and facial expression cues differentially augment spoken sentence and discourse comprehension for acute left and right hemisphere stroke survivors.
summary: Comprehension for spoken sentences and discourse is differentially impacted by left- (LH) and right-hemisphere (RH) brain damage, such as that caused by stroke. Comprehension deficits can have disabling effects on one's ability to process information, participate in everyday life, and create and maintain relationships. This cross-sectional, observational study evaluated differences in sentence- and discourse-level comprehension between LH and RH stroke survivors across different prosodic conditions and examined relationships between comprehension and damage to key LH and RH regions. title: Spinal cord stimulation for cancer pain: a narrative review of mechanistic rationale, clinical integration, and emerging applications.
summary: Pain remains one of the most prevalent symptoms among patients with advanced cancer, with a substantial subset experiencing persistent pain despite optimized pharmacologic management. Although spinal cord stimulation (SCS) has emerged as a potential neuromodulatory option for refractory cancer-related pain, its role within contemporary multidisciplinary cancer pain management remains incompletely defined. This narrative review examines the mechanistic rationale, clinical applications, guideline positioning, and practical implementation of SCS across cancer pain phenotypes. title: Smooth total variation regularization for interference detection and elimination (STRIDE) for MRI.
summary: MRI is increasingly required to operate near electronic devices that emit dynamic electromagnetic interference (EMI). Existing reference-channel EMI removal methods estimate a transfer function between EMI sensors and imaging coils from the measured data alone, and do not use prior knowledge about the structure of MR images. We develop and validate an EMI removal method that uses the inherent spatial smoothness of MR images as an additional prior, demonstrated on a head-only 0.5T scanner. title: Multisystemic Clues and Diagnostic Gaps: A Comparative Analysis of Pediatric Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation Patients.
summary: Congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG) comprise a diverse group of rare inherited metabolic diseases caused by defects in glycan biosynthesis and processing. Since glycoconjugates play a critical role in development and cellular integrity, disruptions in glycosylation can result in a wide range of multisystemic symptoms, often with prominent neurological involvement. Despite their clinical relevance, many CDG cases remain underdiagnosed due to the limited sensitivity of conventional biochemical tests. This study aims to further characterize the clinical, radiologic, and genetic findings. This study retrospectively analyzed nine pediatric patients diagnosed with CDG at a tertiary center.

summary: Differentiating Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA) from Alzheimer's disease (AD) in vivo is challenging due to overlapping amyloid pathology and limited availability sensitivity of hemorrhagic markers in memory clinic settings. summary: Infarct growth occurs in most patients despite successful thrombectomy. title: Developmental shift from hormonal to neural correlates of psychobehavioral problems among early adolescent boys.
summary: Adolescence begins with puberty and involves dynamic hormonal, neural, and social changes. The early-pubertal testosterone surge, particularly in boys, may shape the amygdala, which regulates emotion and behavior. However, it remains unclear how testosterone- and amygdala-related correlates of psychobehavioral problems differ across early adolescence. title: Endovascular stenting of extracranial cervical artery dissections: A two-center study.
summary: Extracranial arterial dissections (EAD) are uncommon in the general population but represent a relatively frequent cause of ischemic stroke in young adults. title: Dynamic functional abnormalities of cerebellar networks in adolescents with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
summary: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) commonly begins during adolescence, yet its neurobiological basis remains unclear. Beyond the classical cortico-striatal framework, the cerebellum has been implicated in cognitive, affective, and motor regulation, relevant to OCD. However, it is unknown whether adolescent OCD involves abnormal dynamic coordination of large-scale cerebellar networks. summary: Magnetically guided microrobots could enable minimally invasive intracranial interventions by navigating CSF spaces without traversing brain parenchyma. title: Brain network changes in patients with glioma-related epilepsy after frontal resection.
summary: Clinical factors such as IDH status, preoperative seizures, and frontal tumor location influence the prognosis of postoperative glioma-related epilepsy (GRE), but the underlying network-level mechanisms remain unclear. title: Morphological subtypes of Chiari malformation type I and clinical outcomes after posterior fossa decompression.
summary: Chiari malformation type I (CM-I) is the most common structural hindbrain defect in humans and causes debilitating headaches and other neurological symptoms frequently requiring surgery. Although patients' brains have heterogeneous shapes, diagnosis is based on a single radiographic measure with only 1 available pathology-directed treatment. The authors sought to determine whether there are distinct morphological subtypes of CM-I and to determine whether patients with different subtypes differ in clinical response to neurosurgical decompression. summary: Progressive multiple sclerosis (PMS) lacks blood-based biomarkers of the neurodegenerative processes driving disability.
